metadata.method_name: TP-G2: factorial discipline x container frame and survivor placement (iteration 10)
metadata.description: Name-scrubbed grid path programs written by Qwen3-32B in a pre-committed 6x6 discipline x container factorial (24 implementable cells, 12 verified programs each), teacher-forced under iteration 9's neutral-twin context; program-state RDMs (Qwen3-8B bf16 block 17, Qwen3-32B NF4 block 33, R1) tested for discipline vs container with partial Spearman, restricted permutations and program bootstrap (G1); survivor families of the five-name ban and covert BFS/DFS placed on the factorial + catalogue frame with iteration 9's geodesic landing code (G2).

deviations.text: Commit #1 split into #1a (cells, prompts, verifiers, all G1/G2 rules and predictions, before wave A), #1b (placed-program family lists with uids and code sha256, before any placed-program state) and #1c (sha256 of g1.py / g2.py / figures.py, before any G1/G2 output on real data and before the factorial freeze is analysed).
F-COV has 136 programs (five-name ban, 9 non-C6 configurations) instead of ~294; the 98 covert programs of the iteration-2 single/multi-name bans are placed as F-COVX (descriptive).

Ran on an RTX 2000 Ada 16 GB with 6 CPUs and 28 GB RAM (plan: RTX A4500). Qwen3-8B keeps 27 blocks (extraction blocks 9-25 odd + 26), Qwen3-32B NF4 keeps 40 blocks (21, 25, 29, 31, 33, 35, 37, 39); primary blocks 17 / 33 unchanged.
HF_HOME was not overridden (run rule: the shared cache is pre-set); the plan's HF_HOME=./hf_cache was not used, so no hf_cache/ exists in the workspace.

exp46 frozen state caches (cache/states/mcode_8b.npz, mcode_32b.npz, geo_*_k15/k10.npz; 0.6 GB) and the dependency's full_data_out.json (96 MB) are read in place; their sha256 is in inputs_manifest.json (in_place). Everything else is copied into inputs/ or src/ / vendor/.

State reproduction of 10 cached iteration-9 programs: hook check exact (max abs diff 0) and n_code_tokens 10/10 equal, but min cosine 0.99981 (8B) / 0.99990 (32B) against the 0.9999 threshold (mean 0.99996 / 0.99998): iteration 9 ran on an RTX 5090, this round on an RTX 2000 Ada (bf16 kernel numerics). Catalogue states are still taken from the iteration-9 cache.

Amendment in COMMIT1a (before wave A): the tracer reads the planted scan-derived GRID2D programs of BFSO, HEUR and COST as OTHER / DFS, so GRID2D discipline checks use the AST signature + a hand read.

RELAX cells have no frontier; their container check is the structure swept every round (2-D arrays / explicit edge list / set of cells) inside a repeat loop, with no deque, heap, popleft, pop(0) or insort.
Thinking off via reasoning.enabled=false plus the Qwen3 '/no_think' suffix (DeepInfra ignores the flag alone; iteration-9 D10); smoke test confirmed 1 reasoning token.

Top-ups: bibfs 12 and iddfs 12 generated; biastar 6 generated + 6 paraphrases; jps 0 of ~100 generated attempts verified, so all 12 JPS programs are paraphrases of the S3 reference jps4.py (no 50% cap for S3-seeded top-ups). JPS placement and frame evidence is therefore reference-derived, low independence.
RELAX-SET reached 11 verified programs at freeze (one hand-read REJECT); above the 10 floor, N flagged.

Hand reads (139 rows in data/hand_reads_v10.jsonl): full programs for the first batches of every hand-read cell; later programs of highly uniform cells (GRID2D, BFSO-SET, IDDFS, BiBFS, BiA*) on their selection-rule / structure lines plus a container grep; JPS paraphrases 3 in full and 9 by jump-helper structure plus heap-push counts equal to the reference. Reasons are recorded per row.

Primary, crossed-core and cell-cluster bootstraps use 1,000 resamples and 2,000 restricted permutations as committed; the sensitivity variants (S3-S7, S10) use 200 program-bootstrap resamples and S2 semi-partial CIs 100, for time (the box was CPU-bound).
A first full G1 run was killed after BLAS oversubscription (load 14 on 6 CPUs) and rerun with one BLAS thread per process; results come from the rerun (same code, same seeds).

T7 synthetic 'discipline-only' states encode the committed D_disc geometry (COST half-way from BFSO) and use noise 0.6; with independent discipline means the tie structure of D_disc caps rho_dc below 0.5.
F-RF has 14 programs (iteration-8 randomized-DFS rows counted as random frontiers) and F-OTH 8 (plan: 13 and 10).
Frame catalogue = 129 iteration-9 M-code PRIMARY programs (frozen states, other GPU) + 48 frozen top-ups (this round); bibfs/iddfs/biastar classes mix both sources.

results/positioning.json is a title-level screen of 6 dated OpenAlex scholarly queries (top results, verdicts occupies/adjacent/irrelevant); verbatim quotes were not fetched (time), so verdicts are provisional.

src/g1.py differs from its COMMIT1c hash only by two lines in synthetic_states (the T7 test generator places COST half-way from BFSO); removing them reproduces the committed sha256 exactly (checked). All statistics functions are as committed; g2.py, r0.py, extract.py, assemble.py, freeze.py and tests/test_analysis.py match their committed hashes.

src/analysis.py (G1/G2 drivers: frame assembly, sensitivity list, subframe filters) was written after COMMIT1c and before any G1/G2 output, implementing COMMIT1a's rules, but was not hash-committed. After a first quick G1 run (whose numbers equal the final ones) only worker counts, BLAS threads and sensitivity bootstrap counts changed. src/figures.py and src/outputs.py were written after the G1/G2 outputs (presentation only), so the planned COMMIT1d did not happen.

examples.input:
CELL BFSO-DEQUE (FIFO / level order x DEQUE); prompt:
Write the search as follows. Keep the frontier in a collections.deque. Add every newly discovered cell at the right end with append() and always take the next cell to expand from the left end with popleft(), so cells are expanded strictly in first-in first-out order. Mark a cell as seen at the moment it is added to the deque and record its parent then. Do not use heapq, a set as the frontier, or recursion.

Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.
